name: BB
resume: All seven exports match BB 2026.1.0 on the spectral-gradient paths. spg can check an analytic gradient with numDeriv. projectLinear calls quadprog solve.QP. BBsolve starts small systems with the same Nelder-Mead simplex as stats::optim. control BFGS=TRUE is the L-BFGS-B fallback in stats::optim and is not translated. There is no crate.

functions.name: spg
functions.done: Birgin, Martinez, and Raydan spectral projected gradient, including the nonmonotone line search.

check.case: Spectral projected gradient. A box constraint is the default projection. An analytic gradient is checked with numDeriv only when checkGrad asks for it.

proof.r:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(BB))
fn <- function(x) sum((x - c(1, 2, 3))^2)
gr <- function(x) 2 * (x - c(1, 2, 3))
one <- function() {
  res <- spg(c(0, 0, 0), fn, gr, control=list(checkGrad=FALSE, trace=FALSE), quiet=TRUE)
  c(res$par, res$value, res$gradient, res$fn.reduction, res$iter, res$feval, res$convergence)
}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
cat(paste(sprintf("%.17g", as.numeric(value)), collapse=","), "
", sep="")
cat("MS
")
cat(sprintf("%.17g
", median(elapsed) * 1000))

functions.name: dfsane
functions.done: DF-SANE with the two-sided nonmonotone line search. NM and BFGS stay off unless control asks for them.

check.case: Derivative-free spectral residual method. Nelder-Mead and L-BFGS-B are optional and off by default.

  res <- dfsane(c(0, 0), sys, control=list(NM=FALSE, BFGS=FALSE, trace=FALSE), quiet=TRUE)
  c(res$par, res$residual, res$fn.reduction, res$feval, res$iter, res$convergence)
}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0

cat(paste(sprintf("%.17g", as.numeric(value)), collapse=","), "

", median(elapsed) * 1000))
proof.python:
import numpy as np
from BB import dfsane
def sys(x):
    return np.array([x[0] - 1.0, x[1] - 2.0])
def one():
    res = dfsane([0.0, 0.0], sys, control={"NM": False, "BFGS": False, "trace": False}, quiet=True)
    return np.array([res["par"][0], res["par"][1], res["residual"], res["fn.reduction"], res["feval"], res["iter"], res["convergence"]])
import statistics
import time
value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
arr = __import__("numpy").atleast_1d(__import__("numpy").asarray(value, dtype=float))
print(",".join("%.17g" % float(v) for v in arr))
print("MS")
print("%.17g" % statistics.median(elapsed))

functions.name: multiStart
functions.done: A vector start becomes one row. Converged is true when the solver reports convergence 0.

check.case: Each row of par is a start. action solve calls BBsolve. action optimize calls BBoptim.

proof.r:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(BB))
sys <- function(x) c(x[1] - 1, x[2] - 2)
one <- function() {
  res <- multiStart(rbind(c(0, 0), c(4, -1)), sys, action="solve", control=list(trace=FALSE, NM=FALSE), quiet=TRUE)
  c(as.vector(res$par), res$fvalue, as.numeric(res$converged))
}

proof.python:
import numpy as np
from BB import multi_start
def sys(x):
    return np.array([x[0] - 1.0, x[1] - 2.0])
def one():
    res = multi_start(np.array([[0.0, 0.0], [4.0, -1.0]]), sys, action="solve", control={"trace": False, "NM": False}, quiet=True)
    par = np.ravel(res["par"], order="F")
    return np.concatenate([par, res["fvalue"], res["converged"].astype(float)])
import statistics

elapsed = []

    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
